column1: # title: ENG-205 Middle Ages Intro — 4 Main Ideas
The time span of the Middle Ages
column2: The Middle Ages in England run from about 450, when the Anglo-Saxons arrived, to about 1485, when the Tudors came to power.

column1: The three periods of medieval English literature
column2: Medieval English literature is divided into the Anglo-Saxon, Anglo-Norman, and Middle English periods.

column1: How the Norman Conquest changed who spoke what
column2: The Norman Conquest of 1066 put a French-speaking ruling class in charge of England.

column1: The four languages of Norman England
column2: After the Conquest, French was used at court, Latin in the Church, English among common people, and Celtic languages at the edges.
English lost status for about 200 years, then returned as Middle English filled with French words.

column1: The return of English to official use
column2: By 1362, English was being used again in the law courts and Parliament.
The heroic code bound a generous lord and his warriors, who owed him loyalty to the death and revenge if he was killed.
Old English poets used kennings, which are compound metaphors such as "life-house" for the body.
Old English poetry is organized by alliteration rather than rhyme.

column1: The tone of Old English poetry
column2: Old English poetry has an elegiac tone that blends pagan heroism with Christian belief.
Chivalric romance grew out of Celtic Breton lays that were popular with Norman aristocrats.
Chivalric romance centers on knightly quests, courtly love, courtesy, and prowess.
The Arthurian tradition runs from Geoffrey of Monmouth to Sir Gawain and the Green Knight to Malory's Morte Darthur.
Caxton printed Malory's Morte Darthur in 1485, which spread the Arthurian stories widely.

column1: The death toll of the Black Death
column2: The Black Death of 1348 killed about a quarter to a third of Europe's population.

column1: How the plague of 1348 led to social mobility
column2: The Black Death caused a severe labor shortage, which allowed surviving workers to demand higher wages and rise in social status.

column1: The rise of the merchant class
column2: After the plague, a merchant class grew in wealth and influence.
Chaucer, a merchant's son, wrote in English for the rising middle class.
Langland's Piers Plowman and Wycliffe's English Bible criticized society and the Church.
The social changes that followed the plague led to the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
The Angles, Saxons, and Jutes brought the Germanic speech that became Old English.
Beowulf shows the heroic code, wergild, and the elegiac tone of Anglo-Saxon culture.
Bede's Ecclesiastical History preserves Caedmon's Hymn, the earliest poem recorded in English.
In Old English verse, any vowel can alliterate with any other vowel.

column1: Word substitution in Old English poetry
column2: Old English poets used synecdoche and metonymy, such as "keel" for a ship and "crown" for the king.
The riddles in the Exeter Book show the Anglo-Saxon love of wordplay and double meanings.
Alliterative verse returned in the 1300s in works such as Sir Gawain and the Green Knight and Piers Plowman.
Anglo-Saxon law replaced blood revenge with wergild, a payment made for killing or injuring someone.
Alfred the Great created the fyrd, England's first national militia.

column1: The Witan as a forerunner of Parliament
column2: The Witan advised Anglo-Saxon kings and later developed toward Parliament.
The shire-reeve ran each shire for the king, and his title became the word "sheriff."
Middle English, the language of Chaucer, followed Old English and was not yet standardized.

column1: The rise of a standard English
column2: In the 1400s, a London and East Midlands form of English became the standard.
The Great Vowel Shift moved English long vowels to new sounds, which is why English spelling no longer matches pronunciation; for example, "bite" was once pronounced like "beet."
Printing helped fix English spelling and moved the language toward Early Modern English.
Medieval English drama included mystery plays, performed in cycles like York and Wakefield, and morality plays such as Everyman.
